threshold.rule: HARD if and only if at least THREE of the five criteria score 3 (the rubric's 'severe, a principal driver of difficulty for this book'). Equivalent in totals: every book with total >= 13 is HARD (13 cannot be reached with fewer than three 3s: 3+3+2+2+2 = 12), and a book at 12 is HARD only when its 12 is composed of three 3s (Acts). A single criterion at 3 does NOT force HARD; it forces that book's extra_scrutiny_focus regions to be carried as FLAGGED REGIONS in its brief (Fable-boss escalation target, final-checker attention, and my recommendation that the no-sampling-shortcut arm apply to those regions even on the STANDARD track). Applied without exception after the two named adjustments.
threshold.rationale: (1) The instrument follows the rubric's own scale words and the owner's words: 'the hardest books' with 'lots of' hard translation, literature, prophecy, connections or contested passages means severe on a MAJORITY of the owner's five axes, not merely present on one. (2) The bare total is the wrong instrument on its own because the prophecy axis is a genre flag: Prophets receive 2-3 on it for free while epistles and narrative receive 0-1, so a total threshold systematically under-routes New Testament books; Acts is severe on three axes and is denied by a total threshold only because prophecy is 1. The total also moves by one point on 1-versus-2 calibration noise that the severe-axis count ignores. (3) 'Any criterion at 3 forces HARD' is rejected: it would route 30 of 42 books HARD (after the two adjustments; 29 before), making the extra-scrutiny track the default and inverting 'hardest'; it is hostage to 2-versus-3 calibration noise across four scorers (Nah 3 / Zeph 2 on translation; Col 3 / Zech 2 on ecclesial), so two comparable books would land on different tracks by scorer accident; and the scorers' own evidence shows single-axis hazards are LOCALISED (they name the stretches), for which the campaign already has an instrument: the flagged-region list, the Fable boss as escalation target and the Fable whole-book final checker, which the STANDARD track keeps under OW-6. Whole-cycle Fable control is for books whose hazard is DIFFUSE, i.e. severe on most axes. (4) Corroboration: the owner-named books Daniel and Revelation are 5/5 severe; Ezekiel is 5/5 severe unnamed; the rule's HARD set is exactly the top 15 of 42 by severe-axis count (6 of the 15 remaining Hebrew books, 9 of the 27 New Testament books). (5) Cost-awareness is recorded, not decisive: the HARD track (CAMPAIGN_CLOSE_GATE item 11) adds a Fable high-effort controlling lane, no-sampling peer and spot coverage on flagged regions, a whole-book final check and a second independent Fable review before close; 15 HARD cycles is a material but bounded increase, and OW-6b(e) keeps upward re-classification open at every Phase 0, so an error toward STANDARD is correctable before a book's boundaries are drawn while an error toward HARD is not refundable.
threshold.single_criterion_consideration: Considered and rejected as a HARD trigger for the reasons in (3); retained as a mandatory flagged-region trigger. Beyond the eleven two-severe-axes books, an any-single-3 rule would also have routed the four single-severe-axis books HARD: Amos (connections, adjusted), Obad (connections), Nah (translation), 1Tim (ecclesial). The books with two severe axes that remain STANDARD are listed in summary.two_severe_axes_standard_books and are the Phase-0 upward re-classification watch list.

greek_substrate_ruling.finding: CONFIRMED from the inputs: no Greek New Testament source text is staged for this campaign. Batch 02: 'which Greek witness the campaign will stage is unknown to me' (Matt) and 'the staged Greek witness is unknown to me' (Mark, Luke, John, Acts, Rom); batch 03 (1Cor): 'the Greek substrate the campaign will stage for the NT is unknown to this scorer'; batch 04 (Heb, Rev): 'the NT Greek substrate lane for this campaign is not named in the documents I was given'. Every NT entry's uncertainty field records its textual claims as unverified against bytes. I did not probe any staging directory (exact-path law); the Hebrew lane's substrate (OSHB/WLC keyed to WEB with declared numbering zones, byte-collate tiers, normalize dry-run, word index, citation sweep) is named in the batches and the ledger, and the ledger's root-cause law records that every shipped-past-reviewer defect class was caught by a deterministic sweep or a byte re-verification lane against that substrate.
greek_substrate_ruling.consequence_for_the_nt_books: The TRACK ruling for the 27 NT books stands on the rubric and is not changed by the substrate question. But no NT book may START its cycle, on either track, until a Greek witness is staged, keyed to WEB verse by verse with verse-existence flags, and its tooling (WEB<->Greek crosswalk, collate tiers byte / accent_stripped / skeleton, normalize dry-run, word index, citation sweep, stray sweep) is built and validated on a fixture. Ground: CAMPAIGN_CLOSE_GATE item 5 makes 'HEBREW/GREEK QUOTE BYTES + TIER LABELS: every original-language splice byte-collated at its cited ref' a hard book-close gate; without a Greek witness that arm is unsatisfiable for any row carrying Greek, and a row carrying no Greek cannot argue a syntax-, formula- or variant-based seam from any tier-1 layer, because the only remaining surface is WEB punctuation and paragraphing, which is tier-4 and barred as a driver (E-23, OW-2 item 5). If the owner nonetheless orders NT books run without a Greek substrate, this artifact re-classifies all 27 NT books HARD (upward re-classification, reason recorded: loss of the deterministic byte-verification layer) and each NT close requires an explicit owner waiver of the item-5 Greek arm in chat; that compensation adds model review but does not restore byte verification, so it is recorded as inferior, not equivalent.
greek_substrate_ruling.what_is_lost_without_it: Concretely, for 27 of the 42 remaining books: (1) the byte re-verification lane itself: classes E-01 (normalize), E-03 (reviewer-prose citation errors), E-04 (byte-valid wrong-token splices) and E-05 (tier overclaims) are caught only by collate against a staged text and would go undetected across the NT; (2) verse-existence and versification crosswalk: WEB (reported Majority-Text base, unverified) prints verses absent from critical editions: Matt 17:21, 18:11, 23:14; Mark 7:16, 9:44, 9:46, 11:26, 15:28, 16:9-20; Luke 17:36, 23:17; John 5:3b-4, 7:53-8:11; Acts 8:37, 15:34, 24:6b-8a, 28:29; Rom 16:24 plus the doxology position; the 1John 5:7-8 Comma content; and verse-division differences at 1Thess 2:6/7, 2Cor 13:12-14 versus 12-13, 3John 14 versus 15 verses, Rev 12:18/13:1: without a keyed Greek witness no row can record which witness its span exists in, the NT analogue of the MT/WEB zone law whose single-space assumption produced the Jer E-03/E-26 instance; (3) every Greek lexeme, variant and hapax claim in row and review prose (pistis Christou, harpagmos, katechon, en touto, hilasterion, hos/theos at 1Tim 3:16) is unverifiable, so the HIGH-YIELD E-03 and E-05 classes run blind; (4) syntax-based seams have no tier-1 layer: Eph 1:3-14 and 1:15-23, 2Thess 1:3-10 and Col 1:3-14 as single sentences; Gal 2:14-21 speech extent; John 3:16-21 and 3:31-36 speech ends; Jas 2:18 interlocutor extent; 1John's en touto direction; Rom 5:1 echomen; the pistos ho logos direction at 1Tim 3:1a and 4:9 and 2Tim 2:11a and Titus 3:8a; writers would be pushed onto WEB sentence and quotation-mark placement, i.e. the E-23 class that shipped the Isa HIGH, systematically across 27 books; (5) formula-based unit onsets are detectable only in Greek tokens (peri de; pistos ho logos; kai egeneto hote etelesen; houtoi eisin; en pneumati), which WEB renders variably; (6) the normalize lane has a Greek analogue (polytonic precomposed versus combining diacritics, final sigma) that cannot exist without a text; (7) LXX-versus-MT alignment for quotation rows in Heb, Rom, 1Pet, Acts and Matt against the closed OT corpus cannot be done ('disclosed, never silently harmonised' per the scorers).
greek_substrate_ruling.my_ruling: (a) A staged Greek substrate is a Phase-0 PRECONDITION for every NT book regardless of track; not optional; the lane must not cross from Mal to Matt without it. (b) WHICH witness is an OWNER decision: it is a project-level source, licence and provenance choice, it binds the scripture-graph beyond this chunking lane, and it is irreversible in effect once NT rows are keyed. My recommendation: stage the Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine Textform (public domain; parsed edition available) as the PRIMARY key-aligned witness, because its verse existence matches the WEB's reported Majority-Text base one-to-one, the way OSHB keyed to WEB with only declared numbering zones; plus the SBLGNT (CC BY 4.0; MorphGNT morphology CC BY-SA) as the SECONDARY witness for critical-text divergence disclosure at every flagged row. NA28/UBS5 (copyrighted) and the Tyndale House GNT (CC BY-NC-ND) are not eligible for an open-licensed project. sequencing_recommendation: Advice only; canonical order is owner-set and unchanged. (2) Hos (14) follows at once, so the three heaviest Hebrew books sit in a row; expect the longest stretch of the campaign there; Joel to Jonah (STANDARD) are the breather; Mic and Hab are small HARD books; Zeph and Hag STANDARD; Zech HARD with its 1:18-2:13 zone; Mal STANDARD and the last Hebrew-substrate book. (3) Decide the Greek substrate NOW (escalation decision B) so staging and tooling run in parallel with the Hebrew books and are validated on a fixture before Matt's Phase 0; Matt is the first NT book and a borderline STANDARD, so run its Phase 0 with the upward re-classification question explicitly open. If the owner prefers a tooling shakedown on a tiny book before Matt, that is an order change (3John, 2John or Phlm first) and needs the owner's ruling; I do not recommend breaking canonical order for it. (4) The NT HARD cluster is front-loaded: Luke, John, Acts, Rom, 1Cor are long HARD books within six consecutive books; budget their second independent Fable reviews as one block, and keep 2Cor (adjusted STANDARD) under its flagged-region list with its Phase-0 re-classification review. (5) 2Thess and 2Pet are small HARD books and cheap; Heb is a long HARD book whose quotation rows depend on the closed OT corpus (LXX-versus-MT disclosure), so its Phase 0 should pull the relevant closed rows. (6) Rev last, with OW-2 item 6's Opus 5 high review plus Fable 5 high adversarial adjudication stacked on the HARD track, followed by the OW-6c end-of-campaign packet. escalation.why: Blast radius is every remaining book: this artifact routes 42 cycles and sets the campaign's cost profile for the rest of the marathon. The owner's words admit two readings that differ by 15 books (severe-on-a-majority = 15 HARD; any-severe-axis = 30 HARD), and OW-5's budget waiver covers only Jeremiah and Lamentations ('for later books the budget law is as the owner sets it'), so the HARD track's cost is the owner's to accept. The Greek substrate question is a project-level source and licence decision outside this lane's authority and is a hard precondition for 27 of the 42 books. Reversibility is partial: upward re-classification is open at every Phase 0, but a book run STANDARD that should have been HARD cannot recover Fable control of its boundaries after they are drawn. No stall: the lane proceeds under this ruling provisionally, because Lam is STANDARD and Ezek and Dan are HARD under every alternative below; Hos is HARD under every alternative except 'owner-named only'; the first book whose track differs across the alternatives is Hos (4th from now) or Joel (5th), which is the owner's decision window.

packet.question: Two decisions. (A) Ratify the HARD/STANDARD rule 'severe (3) on at least three of the five criteria' and its roster (15 HARD: Ezek, Dan, Hos, Mic, Hab, Zech, Luke, John, Acts, Rom, 1Cor, 2Thess, Heb, 2Pet, Rev; 27 STANDARD with flagged regions), or choose another rule from the alternatives. (B) Authorise staging an open-licensed Greek New Testament substrate before any NT book starts, and choose the witness (recommended: Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine primary + SBLGNT secondary).
packet.recommendation: (A) Adopt the three-severe-axes rule as ruled: 15 HARD / 27 STANDARD; every STANDARD book's extra_scrutiny_focus carried as flagged regions with the no-sampling arm applied to those regions; Phase-0 upward re-classification kept open, with 2Cor, Matt, Joel, Mark and Jude as the named watch list; Ezek treated as owner-named-equivalent. (B) Authorise the Greek substrate now: Robinson-Pierpont Byzantine Textform (public domain, WEB-aligned verse existence) as primary witness plus SBLGNT (CC BY 4.0) as secondary for critical-text disclosure; build and validate the Greek tooling during the remaining Hebrew books; licence and edition facts verified at staging; no NT book starts without it.
packet.recommendation_reason: (A) It is the reading of the owner's words that keeps 'hardest' meaning hardest: the HARD set is exactly the books severe on most of the owner's own axes, it includes both owner-named books and the unnamed 15/15 book, it neutralises the prophecy genre flag that a total threshold would let bias routing against the NT, it is robust to the 2-versus-3 scorer noise that an any-single-3 rule is hostage to, and its errors are correctable in the cheap direction (upward at Phase 0). (B) Without a Greek witness the campaign's own hard close gate (item 5, Greek quote bytes) cannot be met, and the deterministic catch layer that found most of the Hebrew books' real defects would not exist for 27 books; a WEB-aligned Byzantine primary gives one-to-one verse keys (no crosswalk gaps in the hazard rows), and a CC BY critical secondary gives the divergence disclosure the scorers demand at every flagged row, both under licences compatible with an open-licensed graph.
